title: The Sleepy Little Owl
summary: Uli is too little to go flying at night with the big owls, and he isn't one bit sleepy. His mum teaches him how to look at the night with his eyes closed.

scenes.text:
In the hollow of an old tree lived a family of owls.

Owls are night animals. When everyone else goes to sleep, they wake up, stretch their wings and fly out.

That night, Dad Owl and the big cousins stepped out onto the branch, ready to go.

Uli stepped out too.

"Not you, Uli," said Dad. "Your wings are still fluff. When they've grown a bit more, you'll come with us."

And off they flew, one after another, without making a sound.

Uli stayed on the branch with his eyes enormous, as round as two saucers.

"Well, I'm not one bit sleepy!" he shouted into the dark.

Mum Owl stayed with him. She sat down beside him and covered him with a wing.

"I'm missing everything," Uli grumbled. "You can't see anything from here. Just black."

"Would you like me to teach you a secret?" said Mum. "It's an old owl's secret."

"What is it?"

"How to look at the night with your eyes closed."

Uli gave her a very serious look.

"Mum. You can't see anything with your eyes closed."

"Try it."

Uli closed his eyes. First one. Then the other.

At first, nothing happened. All black.

"Now, don't look," whispered Mum. "Listen."

Uli listened.

And little by little, things began to come out of the dark. Close by, something was stirring the leaves. Further down, between the stones, water was running.

"I can see a river," said Uli, very softly. "It's shining in the moonlight."

"You see?" said Mum. "You're already looking."

"Listen further away," said Mum.

Uli listened further away. Past the water. Past the forest.

And from very far away, above the lake, came a voice he knew very well.

It was a hoot.

"It's Dad!" said Uli, without opening his eyes. "He's flying over the lake. His wings are spread wide… and now he's going down… and now up again."

Uli could see it all. He could see it better than if he were there.

And he opened his beak in an enormous yawn.

"Listen closer," said Mum.

Uli listened closer. So close, so close, that there was nothing left between the two of them.

Under Mum's wing, warm and slow, beat a heart.

Thump. Thump. Thump.

"Mum," murmured Uli. "The night is very big."

"Very big," she said. "And it will wait for you. When your wings have grown, you'll fly all of it."

Uli didn't answer. He was already asleep.

At dawn, when Dad came home, he found him curled up in a little ball of feathers, snoring.

"Well, look at that," Dad chuckled. "The sleepiest owl in the whole forest."
